svg.title: Hierarchical group_cast: send shared KV once per destination node
svg.desc: One S-byte KV segment owned by source GPU 2, CP rank 2, is required by all eight GPUs on node 1, CP ranks 8 through 15. Flat delivery sends eight copies over the inter-node network, totaling 8S. Hierarchical delivery sends one S-byte copy to GPU 2, CP rank 10, on the destination node; the other seven GPUs obtain the data over NVLink, totaling 7S of local payload. Inter-node payload falls from 8S to S, an 87.5 percent reduction. Across three destination nodes the corresponding totals are 24S and 3S. This is ideal shared-payload accounting, not a measured speedup.
svg.text: Hierarchical communication: send shared KV once
group_cast • one source segment • eight consumer GPUs per destination node
Every destination GPU requests these same bytes.
Send the same KV separately to every consumer.
Send once across nodes; distribute locally.
Same segment, same consumers, fewer bytes across the network
Per destination node: 8S → S. For CP32 with 3 destination nodes: 24S → 3S.
Exact 8× reduction assumes all 8 destination ranks request the same KV segment.
Partial overlap gives a smaller saving. Payload only; excludes protocol overhead and local packing.
group_reduce reverses the pattern: reduce within each node, then send one reduced segment back.
